findingProjection.desc: CHK-002 adversarial:0 was authored from a false premise and one of its two clauses is unsatisfiable on this branch. The intent text reads 'the local d3 hard-failure branch in scripts/build-web.mjs survives the port AND dossier.js is concatenated after app.js, not before'. The d3 hard-failure change exists only as an uncommitted edit in the MAIN checkout; it is not committed on story/B-9f2c and it is not upstream either. Verified two ways: grep -c 'd3 is missing' packages/graph/scripts/build-web.mjs returns 0 on this branch, and the CHK-002 implementer independently reported build-web.mjs is now byte-identical to upstream. So no work on this branch can either satisfy or violate that clause. The load-order clause is the real risk and IS proven: build-web.mjs concatenates app.js at line 33, playback.js at 36 and dossier.js at 40, and the recorded evidence for this intent pins that ordering with a negative control. No evidence was fabricated for the d3 clause; the implementer recorded its voiding in the evidence note. Deliberately NOT fixed by rewriting the intent: verificationIntent is frozen after PLAN by design, and checklist_update correctly refused the edit. Rewriting a frozen intent mid-DEV to match what was actually built is exactly the self-absolution the freeze exists to prevent. Filing this instead so the mismatch is auditable rather than silently reworded.

doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md:111-115 (section 'Test-surface placement') states 'Two test lists in this repository are separately maintained, and neither is a subset of the other: validate.commands in the project config, and test:serial-reference in the root package.json.' This is incomplete: packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts's RESOURCE_POLICY (lines 116-159) is a THIRD fail-closed membership authority -- entriesFromSerialReference (full-suite-runner.ts:216-227) throws 'canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[...]' and aborts the whole suite (called at line 590 of main(), before any test entry is scheduled) if a test:serial-reference member has no RESOURCE_POLICY entry. This story's own CHK-005 checklist context explicitly modeled its plan on this doc's 'TWO separate test-surface lists' framing and, as a direct consequence, registered the new graph-story-flag-smoke task in validate.commands and test:serial-reference but not in RESOURCE_POLICY -- causing npm test to abort in 858ms with exactly the unknownPolicy error the code comments describe, which blocked done_required_validate and forced a TEST->DEV->REVIEW bounce (fixed in commit f4e9acdd21). The code's own comments at full-suite-runner.ts:145-146 and :151-153 record that this identical trap was already hit twice before by other stories (B-49ed, B-cdf6), meaning the canonical decision doc has been silently incomplete across at least three incidents. A future implementer who reads only this doc (as CHK-005 did) will reproduce the same suite-aborting failure. Severity high: this is the specific reproducible-bug-inducing doc gap the review task explicitly asked to check for, and the doc is the canonical decision reference cited by this story's own checklist relatedDocs.

packages/main/src/tasks/graph-story-flag-smoke.ts CHK-005:adversarial:0 pinned command only re-verifies lattice.config.json validate.commands and package.json (test:<name> script + test:serial-reference membership) -- it never reads packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts's RESOURCE_POLICY, the THIRD fail-closed membership authority that was the actual root cause of the done_required_validate failure this round (npm test aborted in 858ms with 'canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[test:graph-story-flag-smoke]', fixed in f4e9acdd21). Negative control on a scratch copy (git show HEAD:packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts with the RESOURCE_POLICY repoRead('test:graph-story-flag-smoke') line at line 159 removed, never touching the tracked file) confirms the pinned adversarial command still prints SELECTOR_BOTH_SURFACES_REGISTERED and exits 0 against the real repo's lattice.config.json/package.json, i.e. it is a false positive for exactly the class of regression it claims to guard against ('the task is registered in BOTH surfaces, so membership in one list is never mistaken for coverage by the other'). The CHK-005 verificationIntent wording is frozen after PLAN so it cannot be reworded now (same disposition as F-001); this finding records the gap so the pinned probe (or a follow-up story) can add a third assertion reading RESOURCE_POLICY membership, matching the corrected 'three membership authorities' text just landed in docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md by F-002. Not blocking: the live defect is already fixed (f4e9acdd21) and independently confirmed by the commit chain through done_required_validate; this is a test-completeness gap in the regression guard, not a currently-failing check.

The d3 hard-failure change exists only as an uncommitted edit in the MAIN checkout; it is not committed on story/B-9f2c and it is not upstream either. Verified two ways: grep -c 'd3 is missing' packages/graph/scripts/build-web.mjs returns 0 on this branch, and the CHK-002 implementer independently reported build-web.mjs is now byte-identical to upstream. So no work on this branch can either satisfy or violate that clause. The load-order clause is the real risk and IS proven: build-web.mjs concatenates app.js at line 33, playback.js at 36 and dossier.js at 40, and the recorded evidence for this intent pins that ordering with a negative control. No evidence was fabricated for the d3 clause; the implementer recorded its voiding in the evidence note. Deliberately NOT fixed by rewriting the intent: verificationIntent is frozen after PLAN by design, and checklist_update correctly refused the edit. Rewriting a frozen intent mid-DEV to match what was actually built is exactly the self-absolution the freeze exists to prevent. Filing this instead so the mismatch is auditable rather than silently reworded.

doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md:111-115 (section 'Test-surface placement') states 'Two test lists in this repository are separately maintained, and neither is a subset of the other: validate.commands in the project config, and test:serial-reference in the root package.json.' This is incomplete: packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts's RESOURCE_POLICY (lines 116-159) is a THIRD fail-closed membership authority -- entriesFromSerialReference (full-suite-runner.ts:216-227) throws 'canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[...]' and aborts the whole suite (called at line 590 of main(), before any test entry is scheduled) if a test:serial-reference member has no RESOURCE_POLICY entry. This story's own CHK-005 checklist context explicitly modeled its plan on this doc's 'TWO separate test-surface lists' framing and, as a direct consequence, registered the new graph-story-flag-smoke task in validate.commands and test:serial-reference but not in RESOURCE_POLICY -- causing npm test to abort in 858ms with exactly the unknownPolicy error the code comments describe, which blocked done_required_validate and forced a TEST->DEV->REVIEW bounce (fixed in commit f4e9acdd21). The code's own comments at full-suite-runner.ts:145-146 and :151-153 record that this identical trap was already hit twice before by other stories (B-49ed, B-cdf6), meaning the canonical decision doc has been silently incomplete across at least three incidents. A future implementer who reads only this doc (as CHK-005 did) will reproduce the same suite-aborting failure. Severity high: this is the specific reproducible-bug-inducing doc gap the review task explicitly asked to check for, and the doc is the canonical decision reference cited by this story's own checklist relatedDocs.

packages/main/src/tasks/graph-story-flag-smoke.ts CHK-005:adversarial:0 pinned command only re-verifies lattice.config.json validate.commands and package.json (test:<name> script + test:serial-reference membership) -- it never reads packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts's RESOURCE_POLICY, the THIRD fail-closed membership authority that was the actual root cause of the done_required_validate failure this round (npm test aborted in 858ms with 'canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[test:graph-story-flag-smoke]', fixed in f4e9acdd21). Negative control on a scratch copy (git show HEAD:packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts with the RESOURCE_POLICY repoRead('test:graph-story-flag-smoke') line at line 159 removed, never touching the tracked file) confirms the pinned adversarial command still prints SELECTOR_BOTH_SURFACES_REGISTERED and exits 0 against the real repo's lattice.config.json/package.json, i.e. it is a false positive for exactly the class of regression it claims to guard against ('the task is registered in BOTH surfaces, so membership in one list is never mistaken for coverage by the other'). The CHK-005 verificationIntent wording is frozen after PLAN so it cannot be reworded now (same disposition as F-001); this finding records the gap so the pinned probe (or a follow-up story) can add a third assertion reading RESOURCE_POLICY membership, matching the corrected 'three membership authorities' text just landed in docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md by F-002. Not blocking: the live defect is already fixed (f4e9acdd21) and independently confirmed by the commit chain through done_required_validate; this is a test-completeness gap in the regression guard, not a currently-failing check.

Recorded on behalf of the test-coverage reviewer, which identified this but could not register it because the review-inventory epoch RIE-004 was already FINALIZED and consumed. Commit dcf54ecff3 adapted verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs to main's new on-demand client build, but its recovery branch was a genuine coverage weakening rather than a pure contract adaptation: the success condition reduced to fs.existsSync(assets/app.html) plus an OR-style output substring match on 'building browser client' or 'graph serving'. It never checked d3.min.js, never checked the served content, and never bound the log line to who produced it. The reviewer proved this with a negative control on a scratchpad copy: feeding the branch's exact logic a fabricated output containing only 'graph serving' with rebuilt=true produced ZERO failures, so a handler writing any bytes to app.html (truncated, stale or corrupt) and logging the right words would pass a check whose entire documented purpose is proving a missing or broken browser client is never silently served. Severity is medium rather than high because production code independently re-checks both app.html and d3.min.js in ensureGraphClientBuilt and throws before any serving line prints, so the gap is not exploitable in isolation; but it would go silent the moment that handler-side check regressed. FIXED rather than deferred, in commit 4912d8390a: the recovery branch now also requires the rebuilt app.html to parse as HTML, to contain openStoryDossier (the inlined shell a real build produces), to not be implausibly small, and to be accompanied by the required d3.min.js bundle. Verified by re-running the reviewer's own scenario: a 42-byte stub with a 'graph serving' line is now CAUGHT on two independent grounds where it previously produced no failures, and npm --prefix packages/graph run check still exits 0.

packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:53-89 (current HEAD, unchanged since 4912d8390a): `rebuilt = fs.existsSync(asset)` (line 53) is sampled once, right after execFileSync's 60s timeout fires, and races the child's own spawnSync(npm run build) inside ensureGraphClientBuilt. Reproduced live in this worktree with the unmodified script: `npm --prefix packages/graph run check` failed at verify-missing-assets-fail with MISSING_ASSET_HANDLING_BROKEN, even though assets/app.html and assets/d3.min.js were both freshly rebuilt (mtimes matched the run within the same second) -- the rebuild genuinely succeeded, just moments after the 60s sample point. Because the script falls into the else (recovery-impossible) branch whenever `rebuilt` samples false, and the SIGKILL cleanup at the bottom only runs `if (rebuilt) { ...kill... } else if (held.length) { ...report... }`, the still-serving graph process was left running and leaked, listening on the port (verified via lsof/ps: PID 45353 for GRAPH_VERIFY_PORT=8819, uncleaned by the script, had to be killed manually). Two concrete effects: (1) the commit's own stated goal -- 'the command must never end up listening while the client is still missing' -- is inverted in this exact scenario: the client WAS built (so nothing is missing), yet the check reports MISSING_ASSET_HANDLING_BROKEN and simultaneously fails to kill or even report the real leaked listener, because that report path is also gated on `!rebuilt`. (2) repeated runs of `npm run check` on a loaded machine will accumulate leaked `node bin/proof-or-stop.js graph --port=8819` processes with no diagnostic pointing at the actual cause (a timing race, not a broken recovery path). This is a genuine, reproduced-twice defect distinct from the assertion-strength gap already fixed in 4912d8390a (content validation of the rebuilt app.html/d3.min.js) -- that fix hardens the `rebuilt===true` branch's assertions but does not touch how `rebuilt` itself is determined, so the race is unaffected by it.

Recorded on behalf of the test-coverage lane, which found it but could not register it because the tree was dirty with the in-flight F-006 fix at the time. Two residual limits in verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs after the F-005 strengthening, both real, neither blocking. (1) DELIBERATE STUB: the recovery branch's four checks (parses as HTML, contains openStoryDossier, at least 100000 bytes, d3.min.js present) can all be satisfied simultaneously by a hand-crafted stub that is padded past the size floor, contains the literal marker string, and is paired with a d3.min.js copied from a stale earlier build. The reviewer demonstrated this on a scratchpad script and it produces zero failures. The F-005 strengthening raised the bar substantially (four content assertions replacing an existsSync-plus-substring match) but did not close it to zero; closing it fully would require deriving the expected content from the build output rather than asserting fixed markers. (2) PRESENT-BUT-STALE IS UNTESTED BY CONSTRUCTION: ensureGraphClientBuilt only rebuilds when app.html or d3.min.js is MISSING (`if (existsSync(appHtml) && existsSync(d3Bundle)) return;` at handlers/graph.ts:81) and never checks staleness against current source, while this verifier only exercises the path where app.html was renamed away. So a present-but-stale client is outside what this script can observe, by design of both sides rather than by oversight. DEFERRED per CLAUDE.md defect triage rather than fixed: low severity, not a regression of this story's acceptance scope, and not gate-distorting, because production code independently re-checks both files before returning and the shipped CLI cannot reach the stub scenario without someone deliberately fabricating assets. Follow-up for a dedicated story: assert the rebuilt page against a digest derived from the build inputs instead of fixed markers, and decide separately whether ensureGraphClientBuilt should detect staleness rather than only absence.

CHK-002 adversarial:0 was authored from a false premise and one of its two clauses is unsatisfiable on this branch. The d3 hard-failure change exists only as an uncommitted edit in the MAIN checkout; it is not committed on story/B-9f2c and it is not upstream either. So no work on this branch can either satisfy or violate that clause. The load-order clause is the real risk and IS proven: build-web.mjs concatenates app.js at line 33, playback.js at 36 and dossier.js at 40, and the recorded evidence for this intent pins that ordering with a negative control. Deliberately NOT fixed by rewriting the intent: verificationIntent is frozen after PLAN by design, and checklist_update correctly refused the edit. Rewriting a frozen intent mid-DEV to match what was actually built is exactly the self-absolution the freeze exists to prevent. Filing this instead so the mismatch is auditable rather than silently reworded.

Commit dcf54ecff3 adapted verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs to main's new on-demand client build, but its recovery branch was a genuine coverage weakening rather than a pure contract adaptation: the success condition reduced to fs.existsSync(assets/app.html) plus an OR-style output substring match on 'building browser client' or 'graph serving'. FIXED rather than deferred, in commit 4912d8390a: the recovery branch now also requires the rebuilt app.html to parse as HTML, to contain openStoryDossier (the inlined shell a real build produces), to not be implausibly small, and to be accompanied by the required d3.min.js bundle. packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:53-89 (current HEAD, unchanged since 4912d8390a): `rebuilt = fs.existsSync(asset)` (line 53) is sampled once, right after execFileSync's 60s timeout fires, and races the child's own spawnSync(npm run build) inside ensureGraphClientBuilt. Reproduced live in this worktree with the unmodified script: `npm --prefix packages/graph run check` failed at verify-missing-assets-fail with MISSING_ASSET_HANDLING_BROKEN, even though assets/app.html and assets/d3.min.js were both freshly rebuilt (mtimes matched the run within the same second) -- the rebuild genuinely succeeded, just moments after the 60s sample point. Because the script falls into the else (recovery-impossible) branch whenever `rebuilt` samples false, and the SIGKILL cleanup at the bottom only runs `if (rebuilt) { ...kill... } else if (held.length) { ...report... }`, the still-serving graph process was left running and leaked, listening on the port (verified via lsof/ps: PID 45353 for GRAPH_VERIFY_PORT=8819, uncleaned by the script, had to be killed manually). (2) repeated runs of `npm run check` on a loaded machine will accumulate leaked `node bin/proof-or-stop.js graph --port=8819` processes with no diagnostic pointing at the actual cause (a timing race, not a broken recovery path). packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:64-79 -- the F-006 kill-before-sample fix only detects and stops a process BOUND TO PORT (lsof -ti:PORT filtered by ps command-line). ensureGraphClientBuilt (packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:83-117) runs npm run build via a SYNCHRONOUS spawnSync inside the outer `node bin/proof-or-stop.js graph` process, before that process ever reaches startServer/binds PORT. If execFileSync's 60s timeout fires while the outer process is still blocked in that spawnSync, the outer (direct) child is SIGTERM'd but the nested npm/build grandchild is NOT -- it is orphaned and keeps running/writing files. Because it never bound PORT, listeners() returns [], leaked.length is 0, the settle sleep `if (leaked.length) execFileSync('sleep',['1'])` is skipped entirely, and `rebuilt = fs.existsSync(asset)` is sampled with zero delay while the orphan may still be mid-write to assets/app.html. This is materially reachable: npm run build for packages/graph is `tsc && node scripts/build-web.mjs`, and a first run is additionally gated by a preceding `npm install` under the SAME 60s budget, so a slow/loaded machine or cold-cache first run can plausibly still be inside that spawnSync at the 60s mark. Recorded on behalf of the test-coverage reviewer, which identified this but could not register it because the review-inventory epoch RIE-004 was already FINALIZED and consumed. Commit dcf54ecff3 adapted verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs to main's new on-demand client build, but its recovery branch was a genuine coverage weakening rather than a pure contract adaptation: the success condition reduced to fs.existsSync(assets/app.html) plus an OR-style output substring match on 'building browser client' or 'graph serving'. It never checked d3.min.js, never checked the served content, and never bound the log line to who produced it. The reviewer proved this with a negative control on a scratchpad copy: feeding the branch's exact logic a fabricated output containing only 'graph serving' with rebuilt=true produced ZERO failures, so a handler writing any bytes to app.html (truncated, stale or corrupt) and logging the right words would pass a check whose entire documented purpose is proving a missing or broken browser client is never silently served. Severity is medium rather than high because production code independently re-checks both app.html and d3.min.js in ensureGraphClientBuilt and throws before any serving line prints, so the gap is not exploitable in isolation; but it would go silent the moment that handler-side check regressed. FIXED rather than deferred, in commit 4912d8390a: the recovery branch now also requires the rebuilt app.html to parse as HTML, to contain openStoryDossier (the inlined shell a real build produces), to not be implausibly small, and to be accompanied by the required d3.min.js bundle. Verified by re-running the reviewer's own scenario: a 42-byte stub with a 'graph serving' line is now CAUGHT on two independent grounds where it previously produced no failures, and npm --prefix packages/graph run check still exits 0.

packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:53-89 (current HEAD, unchanged since 4912d8390a): `rebuilt = fs.existsSync(asset)` (line 53) is sampled once, right after execFileSync's 60s timeout fires, and races the child's own spawnSync(npm run build) inside ensureGraphClientBuilt. Reproduced live in this worktree with the unmodified script: `npm --prefix packages/graph run check` failed at verify-missing-assets-fail with MISSING_ASSET_HANDLING_BROKEN, even though assets/app.html and assets/d3.min.js were both freshly rebuilt (mtimes matched the run within the same second) -- the rebuild genuinely succeeded, just moments after the 60s sample point. Because the script falls into the else (recovery-impossible) branch whenever `rebuilt` samples false, and the SIGKILL cleanup at the bottom only runs `if (rebuilt) { ...kill... } else if (held.length) { ...report... }`, the still-serving graph process was left running and leaked, listening on the port (verified via lsof/ps: PID 45353 for GRAPH_VERIFY_PORT=8819, uncleaned by the script, had to be killed manually). packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:64-79 -- the F-006 kill-before-sample fix only detects and stops a process BOUND TO PORT (lsof -ti:PORT filtered by ps command-line). ensureGraphClientBuilt (packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:83-117) runs npm run build via a SYNCHRONOUS spawnSync inside the outer `node bin/proof-or-stop.js graph` process, before that process ever reaches startServer/binds PORT. If execFileSync's 60s timeout fires while the outer process is still blocked in that spawnSync, the outer (direct) child is SIGTERM'd but the nested npm/build grandchild is NOT -- it is orphaned and keeps running/writing files. Because it never bound PORT, listeners() returns [], leaked.length is 0, the settle sleep `if (leaked.length) execFileSync('sleep',['1'])` is skipped entirely, and `rebuilt = fs.existsSync(asset)` is sampled with zero delay while the orphan may still be mid-write to assets/app.html. This is materially reachable: npm run build for packages/graph is `tsc && node scripts/build-web.mjs`, and a first run is additionally gated by a preceding `npm install` under the SAME 60s budget, so a slow/loaded machine or cold-cache first run can plausibly still be inside that spawnSync at the 60s mark. This is materially reachable: npm run build for packages/graph is `tsc && node scripts/build-web.mjs`, and a first run is additionally gated by a preceding `npm install` under the SAME 60s budget, so a slow/loaded machine or cold-cache first run can plausibly still be inside that spawnSync at the 60s mark. It never checked d3.min.js, never checked the served content, and never bound the log line to who produced it. The reviewer proved this with a negative control on a scratchpad copy: feeding the branch's exact logic a fabricated output containing only 'graph serving' with rebuilt=true produced ZERO failures, so a handler writing any bytes to app.html (truncated, stale or corrupt) and logging the right words would pass a check whose entire documented purpose is proving a missing or broken browser client is never silently served. Severity is medium rather than high because production code independently re-checks both app.html and d3.min.js in ensureGraphClientBuilt and throws before any serving line prints, so the gap is not exploitable in isolation; but it would go silent the moment that handler-side check regressed. FIXED rather than deferred, in commit 4912d8390a: the recovery branch now also requires the rebuilt app.html to parse as HTML, to contain openStoryDossier (the inlined shell a real build produces), to not be implausibly small, and to be accompanied by the required d3.min.js bundle. Verified by re-running the reviewer's own scenario: a 42-byte stub with a 'graph serving' line is now CAUGHT on two independent grounds where it previously produced no failures, and npm --prefix packages/graph run check still exits 0.

packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:53-89 (current HEAD, unchanged since 4912d8390a): `rebuilt = fs.existsSync(asset)` (line 53) is sampled once, right after execFileSync's 60s timeout fires, and races the child's own spawnSync(npm run build) inside ensureGraphClientBuilt. Reproduced live in this worktree with the unmodified script: `npm --prefix packages/graph run check` failed at verify-missing-assets-fail with MISSING_ASSET_HANDLING_BROKEN, even though assets/app.html and assets/d3.min.js were both freshly rebuilt (mtimes matched the run within the same second) -- the rebuild genuinely succeeded, just moments after the 60s sample point. Because the script falls into the else (recovery-impossible) branch whenever `rebuilt` samples false, and the SIGKILL cleanup at the bottom only runs `if (rebuilt) { ...kill... } else if (held.length) { ...report... }`, the still-serving graph process was left running and leaked, listening on the port (verified via lsof/ps: PID 45353 for GRAPH_VERIFY_PORT=8819, uncleaned by the script, had to be killed manually). Two concrete effects: (1) the commit's own stated goal -- 'the command must never end up listening while the client is still missing' -- is inverted in this exact scenario: the client WAS built (so nothing is missing), yet the check reports MISSING_ASSET_HANDLING_BROKEN and simultaneously fails to kill or even report the real leaked listener, because that report path is also gated on `!rebuilt`. (2) repeated runs of `npm run check` on a loaded machine will accumulate leaked `node bin/proof-or-stop.js graph --port=8819` processes with no diagnostic pointing at the actual cause (a timing race, not a broken recovery path). This is a genuine, reproduced-twice defect distinct from the assertion-strength gap already fixed in 4912d8390a (content validation of the rebuilt app.html/d3.min.js) -- that fix hardens the `rebuilt===true` branch's assertions but does not touch how `rebuilt` itself is determined, so the race is unaffected by it.

Recorded on behalf of the test-coverage lane, which found it but could not register it because the tree was dirty with the in-flight F-006 fix at the time. Two residual limits in verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs after the F-005 strengthening, both real, neither blocking. (1) DELIBERATE STUB: the recovery branch's four checks (parses as HTML, contains openStoryDossier, at least 100000 bytes, d3.min.js present) can all be satisfied simultaneously by a hand-crafted stub that is padded past the size floor, contains the literal marker string, and is paired with a d3.min.js copied from a stale earlier build. The reviewer demonstrated this on a scratchpad script and it produces zero failures. The F-005 strengthening raised the bar substantially (four content assertions replacing an existsSync-plus-substring match) but did not close it to zero; closing it fully would require deriving the expected content from the build output rather than asserting fixed markers. (2) PRESENT-BUT-STALE IS UNTESTED BY CONSTRUCTION: ensureGraphClientBuilt only rebuilds when app.html or d3.min.js is MISSING (`if (existsSync(appHtml) && existsSync(d3Bundle)) return;` at handlers/graph.ts:81) and never checks staleness against current source, while this verifier only exercises the path where app.html was renamed away. So a present-but-stale client is outside what this script can observe, by design of both sides rather than by oversight. DEFERRED per CLAUDE.md defect triage rather than fixed: low severity, not a regression of this story's acceptance scope, and not gate-distorting, because production code independently re-checks both files before returning and the shipped CLI cannot reach the stub scenario without someone deliberately fabricating assets. packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:64-79 -- the F-006 kill-before-sample fix only detects and stops a process BOUND TO PORT (lsof -ti:PORT filtered by ps command-line). ensureGraphClientBuilt (packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:83-117) runs npm run build via a SYNCHRONOUS spawnSync inside the outer `node bin/proof-or-stop.js graph` process, before that process ever reaches startServer/binds PORT. If execFileSync's 60s timeout fires while the outer process is still blocked in that spawnSync, the outer (direct) child is SIGTERM'd but the nested npm/build grandchild is NOT -- it is orphaned and keeps running/writing files. Because it never bound PORT, listeners() returns [], leaked.length is 0, the settle sleep `if (leaked.length) execFileSync('sleep',['1'])` is skipped entirely, and `rebuilt = fs.existsSync(asset)` is sampled with zero delay while the orphan may still be mid-write to assets/app.html. Verified live with two independent, exact-shape reproductions of the underlying Node.js semantic (execFileSync's timeout signal reaches only the direct child, never a nested spawnSync grandchild): outer killed at 500ms via SIGTERM, nested spawnSync-invoked shell (blocking the direct child exactly as ensureGraphClientBuilt's spawnSync(npm,['run','build']) does) wrote its marker file ~3s later, well after the outer execFileSync had already thrown -- the marker did not exist immediately after the outer call returned. This is materially reachable: npm run build for packages/graph is `tsc && node scripts/build-web.mjs`, and a first run is additionally gated by a preceding `npm install` under the SAME 60s budget, so a slow/loaded machine or cold-cache first run can plausibly still be inside that spawnSync at the 60s mark. F-006's commit message and finding text claim the RACE half is closed by reordering to kill-before-sample, but that only holds for the sub-case the reviewer's own live repro happened to hit (pid 45353 already bound to port 8819, i.e. timeout fired AFTER ensureGraphClientBuilt returned and startServer was reached) -- not for the sub-case where the timeout fires DURING the build, before any port is bound. The LEAK half of F-006 is correctly and fully fixed (cleanup is no longer gated behind `if (rebuilt)`, and it now correctly finds/kills any process that DID bind the port); the RACE half remains open specifically for the pre-bind (mid-build) timeout window, which is a materially different failure window than F-006's own reproduction covered.

packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:94-97 (fixed by 0c9253c5be) -- the new settle polls fs.existsSync(asset) only, which becomes true as soon as build-web.mjs writeFileSync (build-web.mjs:44) open()s the file (O_CREAT/O_TRUNC), not once the write is complete. This is a distinct failure mode from F-007 (deliberate padded-stub forgery / present-but-stale-not-rebuilt): here a NON-adversarial torn write from the SAME orphaned-build race the commit documents -- SIGTERM reaches only the direct execFileSync child, so the nested npm run build can still be mid-writeFileSync when polled by the unrelated verifier process -- can in principle be sampled while assets/app.html exists but is truncated. The downstream content assertions (lines 115 doctype, 119 openStoryDossier, 122 100KB floor) meaningfully narrow the window: the doctype is the first bytes written and openStoryDossier is emitted last (dossier.js is concatenated after app.js/playback.js at build-web.mjs:39-40, confirmed by tail -c 200 on the built asset), so a write torn strictly before completion is likely, though not certainly (write(2) is permitted a short write at any byte boundary; Node's internal writeFileSync loop can issue more than one write syscall for a ~487KB buffer), to fail the openStoryDossier or size check. Recorded on behalf of the test-coverage reviewer, which identified this but could not register it because the review-inventory epoch RIE-004 was already FINALIZED and consumed. Commit dcf54ecff3 adapted verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs to main's new on-demand client build, but its recovery branch was a genuine coverage weakening rather than a pure contract adaptation: the success condition reduced to fs.existsSync(assets/app.html) plus an OR-style output substring match on 'building browser client' or 'graph serving'. It never checked d3.min.js, never checked the served content, and never bound the log line to who produced it. The reviewer proved this with a negative control on a scratchpad copy: feeding the branch's exact logic a fabricated output containing only 'graph serving' with rebuilt=true produced ZERO failures, so a handler writing any bytes to app.html (truncated, stale or corrupt) and logging the right words would pass a check whose entire documented purpose is proving a missing or broken browser client is never silently served. Severity is medium rather than high because production code independently re-checks both app.html and d3.min.js in ensureGraphClientBuilt and throws before any serving line prints, so the gap is not exploitable in isolation; but it would go silent the moment that handler-side check regressed. FIXED rather than deferred, in commit 4912d8390a: the recovery branch now also requires the rebuilt app.html to parse as HTML, to contain openStoryDossier (the inlined shell a real build produces), to not be implausibly small, and to be accompanied by the required d3.min.js bundle. Verified by re-running the reviewer's own scenario: a 42-byte stub with a 'graph serving' line is now CAUGHT on two independent grounds where it previously produced no failures, and npm --prefix packages/graph run check still exits 0.

Reproduced live in this worktree with the unmodified script: `npm --prefix packages/graph run check` failed at verify-missing-assets-fail with MISSING_ASSET_HANDLING_BROKEN, even though assets/app.html and assets/d3.min.js were both freshly rebuilt (mtimes matched the run within the same second) -- the rebuild genuinely succeeded, just moments after the 60s sample point. Because the script falls into the else (recovery-impossible) branch whenever `rebuilt` samples false, and the SIGKILL cleanup at the bottom only runs `if (rebuilt) { ...kill... } else if (held.length) { ...report... }`, the still-serving graph process was left running and leaked, listening on the port (verified via lsof/ps: PID 45353 for GRAPH_VERIFY_PORT=8819, uncleaned by the script, had to be killed manually). packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:64-79 -- the F-006 kill-before-sample fix only detects and stops a process BOUND TO PORT (lsof -ti:PORT filtered by ps command-line). ensureGraphClientBuilt (packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:83-117) runs npm run build via a SYNCHRONOUS spawnSync inside the outer `node bin/proof-or-stop.js graph` process, before that process ever reaches startServer/binds PORT. If execFileSync's 60s timeout fires while the outer process is still blocked in that spawnSync, the outer (direct) child is SIGTERM'd but the nested npm/build grandchild is NOT -- it is orphaned and keeps running/writing files. Because it never bound PORT, listeners() returns [], leaked.length is 0, the settle sleep `if (leaked.length) execFileSync('sleep',['1'])` is skipped entirely, and `rebuilt = fs.existsSync(asset)` is sampled with zero delay while the orphan may still be mid-write to assets/app.html. This is materially reachable: npm run build for packages/graph is `tsc && node scripts/build-web.mjs`, and a first run is additionally gated by a preceding `npm install` under the SAME 60s budget, so a slow/loaded machine or cold-cache first run can plausibly still be inside that spawnSync at the 60s mark. Two concrete effects: (1) the commit's own stated goal -- 'the command must never end up listening while the client is still missing' -- is inverted in this exact scenario: the client WAS built (so nothing is missing), yet the check reports MISSING_ASSET_HANDLING_BROKEN and simultaneously fails to kill or even report the real leaked listener, because that report path is also gated on `!rebuilt`. (2) repeated runs of `npm run check` on a loaded machine will accumulate leaked `node bin/proof-or-stop.js graph --port=8819` processes with no diagnostic pointing at the actual cause (a timing race, not a broken recovery path). This is a genuine, reproduced-twice defect distinct from the assertion-strength gap already fixed in 4912d8390a (content validation of the rebuilt app.html/d3.min.js) -- that fix hardens the `rebuilt===true` branch's assertions but does not touch how `rebuilt` itself is determined, so the race is unaffected by it.

Recorded on behalf of the test-coverage lane, which found it but could not register it because the tree was dirty with the in-flight F-006 fix at the time. Two residual limits in verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs after the F-005 strengthening, both real, neither blocking. (1) DELIBERATE STUB: the recovery branch's four checks (parses as HTML, contains openStoryDossier, at least 100000 bytes, d3.min.js present) can all be satisfied simultaneously by a hand-crafted stub that is padded past the size floor, contains the literal marker string, and is paired with a d3.min.js copied from a stale earlier build. The reviewer demonstrated this on a scratchpad script and it produces zero failures. The F-005 strengthening raised the bar substantially (four content assertions replacing an existsSync-plus-substring match) but did not close it to zero; closing it fully would require deriving the expected content from the build output rather than asserting fixed markers. (2) PRESENT-BUT-STALE IS UNTESTED BY CONSTRUCTION: ensureGraphClientBuilt only rebuilds when app.html or d3.min.js is MISSING (`if (existsSync(appHtml) && existsSync(d3Bundle)) return;` at handlers/graph.ts:81) and never checks staleness against current source, while this verifier only exercises the path where app.html was renamed away. So a present-but-stale client is outside what this script can observe, by design of both sides rather than by oversight. DEFERRED per CLAUDE.md defect triage rather than fixed: low severity, not a regression of this story's acceptance scope, and not gate-distorting, because production code independently re-checks both files before returning and the shipped CLI cannot reach the stub scenario without someone deliberately fabricating assets. Follow-up for a dedicated story: assert the rebuilt page against a digest derived from the build inputs instead of fixed markers, and decide separately whether ensureGraphClientBuilt should detect staleness rather than only absence.

packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:64-79 -- the F-006 kill-before-sample fix only detects and stops a process BOUND TO PORT (lsof -ti:PORT filtered by ps command-line). ensureGraphClientBuilt (packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:83-117) runs npm run build via a SYNCHRONOUS spawnSync inside the outer `node bin/proof-or-stop.js graph` process, before that process ever reaches startServer/binds PORT. If execFileSync's 60s timeout fires while the outer process is still blocked in that spawnSync, the outer (direct) child is SIGTERM'd but the nested npm/build grandchild is NOT -- it is orphaned and keeps running/writing files. Because it never bound PORT, listeners() returns [], leaked.length is 0, the settle sleep `if (leaked.length) execFileSync('sleep',['1'])` is skipped entirely, and `rebuilt = fs.existsSync(asset)` is sampled with zero delay while the orphan may still be mid-write to assets/app.html. Verified live with two independent, exact-shape reproductions of the underlying Node.js semantic (execFileSync's timeout signal reaches only the direct child, never a nested spawnSync grandchild): outer killed at 500ms via SIGTERM, nested spawnSync-invoked shell (blocking the direct child exactly as ensureGraphClientBuilt's spawnSync(npm,['run','build']) does) wrote its marker file ~3s later, well after the outer execFileSync had already thrown -- the marker did not exist immediately after the outer call returned. This is materially reachable: npm run build for packages/graph is `tsc && node scripts/build-web.mjs`, and a first run is additionally gated by a preceding `npm install` under the SAME 60s budget, so a slow/loaded machine or cold-cache first run can plausibly still be inside that spawnSync at the 60s mark. F-006's commit message and finding text claim the RACE half is closed by reordering to kill-before-sample, but that only holds for the sub-case the reviewer's own live repro happened to hit (pid 45353 already bound to port 8819, i.e. timeout fired AFTER ensureGraphClientBuilt returned and startServer was reached) -- not for the sub-case where the timeout fires DURING the build, before any port is bound. The LEAK half of F-006 is correctly and fully fixed (cleanup is no longer gated behind `if (rebuilt)`, and it now correctly finds/kills any process that DID bind the port); the RACE half remains open specifically for the pre-bind (mid-build) timeout window, which is a materially different failure window than F-006's own reproduction covered.

packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:94-97 (fixed by 0c9253c5be) -- the new settle polls fs.existsSync(asset) only, which becomes true as soon as build-web.mjs writeFileSync (build-web.mjs:44) open()s the file (O_CREAT/O_TRUNC), not once the write is complete. This is a distinct failure mode from F-007 (deliberate padded-stub forgery / present-but-stale-not-rebuilt): here a NON-adversarial torn write from the SAME orphaned-build race the commit documents -- SIGTERM reaches only the direct execFileSync child, so the nested npm run build can still be mid-writeFileSync when polled by the unrelated verifier process -- can in principle be sampled while assets/app.html exists but is truncated. The downstream content assertions (lines 115 doctype, 119 openStoryDossier, 122 100KB floor) meaningfully narrow the window: the doctype is the first bytes written and openStoryDossier is emitted last (dossier.js is concatenated after app.js/playback.js at build-web.mjs:39-40, confirmed by tail -c 200 on the built asset), so a write torn strictly before completion is likely, though not certainly (write(2) is permitted a short write at any byte boundary; Node's internal writeFileSync loop can issue more than one write syscall for a ~487KB buffer), to fail the openStoryDossier or size check. But existsSync alone proves nothing about write-completeness, and the poll never re-checks stability across two samples (e.g. two existsSync+statSync(size) reads separated by one interval, requiring the size to stop changing) before accepting the file as rebuilt. The residual is real but narrower than F-007's two named gaps, since it requires timing an orphaned-build's write() boundary rather than deliberate stub construction.
